clue.text: Among French articles supporting present to sailor, it's beyond absolution

indicators.note: the other pieces sit among the two French articles, which surround them

parts.note: UN and LE are French articles, indefinite and definite
to support a cause is to be for it
to present is to give
AB, able-bodied seaman, is a sailor

explanation.surface: Someone whose gift-giving among the French to a sailor is a sin too grave to forgive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supporting' looks like it describes the articles' role, but it is the word for 'for', as in supporting a cause.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that cannot be pardoned or absolved is by definition unpardonable.

clue.text: Shady glen with one fellow not taking care

indicators.note: shady suggests something dodgy or crooked, so the letters are twisted out of order

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
a fellow is a gent

explanation.surface: A careless man loafs about in a shady glen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shady' looks like it describes the glen, but it signals the rearrangement of that word plus the one.
explanation.definitionFit: Being negligent means failing to take proper care, a synonym in adjectival form.

clue.text: Handy to get oxygen to melt

parts.note: O is the chemical symbol for oxygen
to fuse is to melt together

explanation.surface: Oxygen is useful for getting something to melt.
explanation.definitionFit: Something handy is useful, the same meaning as this phrase.

clue.text: Take in cookhouse on the top floor

indicators.note: the take abbreviation is placed in the cookhouse word

parts.note: a galley is a ship's kitchen or cookhouse
R, for Latin recipe, means take, as on a prescription

explanation.surface: An instruction to carry food into the kitchen upstairs.
explanation.walkthrough: R is the old prescription abbreviation for 'take' (Latin recipe).
explanation.definitionFit: In a theatre the gallery is the highest level of seating, the top floor of the house.

clue.text: A lot of worms pause for thought, being previously exhibited in the 15 square 4

indicators.note: a lot of a word means most of it, with the final letter removed

parts.note: Vermes is the old zoological name for worms as a group
er is the hesitation sound made while thinking

explanation.surface: Worms hesitate before going on show in a famous London gallery.
explanation.walkthrough: 15 square 4 is Trafalgar Square Gallery, the National Gallery in London, which had held a Vermeer exhibition.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dutch painter Johannes Vermeer was the subject of an exhibition at the National Gallery on Trafalgar Square.

clue.text: An inclination a friend has to be Protestant?

parts.note: taken as written
a tip is a slope or inclination
a pal is a friend

explanation.surface: Someone leaning towards a friend's views turns out to be a Protestant.
explanation.definitionFit: A Protestant is, broadly, against the Pope, which is what this adjective means; the question mark admits the stretch.

clue.text: The world of French, not of fruit

indicators.note: not tells us to leave out the following word's French form

parts.note: le monde is French for the world
de is French for of

explanation.surface: A grand claim that the whole French world has nothing to do with fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: The French theme carries over: 'of' is taken in French as DE, and removed from LE MONDE.
explanation.definitionFit: A lemon is a citrus fruit, a straightforward example.

parts.note: the single printed symbol is a punctuation mark ending a parenthetical aside, read as a name for itself

explanation.definitionFit: The printed mark is the closing half of a pair of round brackets, so naming it describes it.

clue.text: Filling place for head removed from hospital, rotten, to be reformed

indicators.note: reformed means made over in a new shape, so the letters are rearranged
the head of the word hospital, its first letter, is taken away

explanation.surface: A rotten hospital needs a new head and a thorough reform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head removed from' leaves OSPITAL; 'to be reformed' shuffles OSPITAL with ROTTEN.
explanation.definitionFit: A filling place is where cars are filled with fuel, a garage forecourt.

clue.text: On one hitting that way, I should be busy on April 1st

definitions.text: I should be busy on April 1st

parts.note: in cricket the on side is also called the leg side
a batsman playing the pull shot sends the ball to the leg side

explanation.surface: A batsman who hits to leg should be busy on April Fools' Day.
explanation.walkthrough: Cricket: the on side is the leg side, and a pull shot is hit to it.
explanation.definitionFit: A prankster who teases people is busiest on April Fools' Day, a playful definition.

clue.text: Classical beauty spot invokes cutting mood

indicators.note: cutting a word here means trimming its final letter

parts.note: temper is a mood, as in a good or bad temper

explanation.surface: A lovely classical place inspires a sharp temper.
explanation.definitionFit: The Vale of Tempe in Thessaly was celebrated by ancient poets as a place of great beauty.

clue.text: An ear for future agenda?

definitions.meaning: the ... of grain on a cereal plant, the head of wheat or barley
an upright pin on a desk onto which papers are pushed to await later attention

explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both a grain head and a spindle for papers awaiting action.

clue.text: Look at the first person in surprise

parts.note: to eye is to look at
the opener is the first person to bat or speak

explanation.surface: Seeing the first person to arrive is quite a surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: Something revealing and unexpected is a surprise, an idiomatic synonym.

clue.text: Imperfectly speaking, exhibit by the Royal Academy …

indicators.note: the words are put on show in a new arrangement, displayed differently

parts.note: RA stands for the Royal Academy of Arts in London

explanation.surface: A halting voice describes an exhibition at the Royal Academy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exhibit' rearranges BY THE with RA; the ellipsis leads into the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A breathy voice lets air escape audibly, an imperfect way of speaking.

clue.text: Battle time for service on much of Portuguese coast

parts.note: the RAF, Royal Air Force, is one of the armed services

indicators.note: much of a word means most of it, its end letters dropped

parts.note: the Algarve is the southern coast of Portugal

explanation.surface: Time for military service along the Portuguese coast in a famous battle.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1805 naval battle off Cape Trafalgar in Spain, Nelson's victory, is an example of a battle.

clue.text: … which could be a help to one recently exhibited in the 15 square 4

definitions.text: one recently exhibited in the 15 square 4

parts.note: which refers back to the Royal Academy in the previous clue, abbreviated RA

indicators.note: could be signals that the words might be rearranged into another form

explanation.surface: The Royal Academy helps an artist recently shown in the National Gallery.
explanation.walkthrough: 15 square 4 is Trafalgar Square Gallery, the National Gallery, which held a Raphael exhibition.
explanation.definitionFit: The Renaissance painter Raphael was the subject of an exhibition at the National Gallery.

clue.text: National rating, one other

indicators.note: other suggests the letters are made into a different form

explanation.surface: A national rating given to one more thing.
explanation.definitionFit: A citizen or native of Argentina is a national of that country, in Spanish form.

clue.text: Draw an abstainer to right performance

parts.note: an gives the letter A
TT, teetotal, describes an abstainer from alcohol
an act is a performance

explanation.surface: Bringing a teetotaller to a good performance.
explanation.definitionFit: To draw a crowd is to attract it, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Cooking — try mash — current in Anglo Saxon times

definitions.note: current here means currency, money in circulation

indicators.note: cooking implies mixing ingredients, so these letters are stirred up

explanation.surface: A kitchen tip for preparing mash, said to date from Anglo-Saxon times.
explanation.definitionFit: A thrymsa was a small gold coin in circulation in Anglo-Saxon England.

clue.text: Source of good food at good height gives pleasure

parts.note: a deli, delicatessen, sells fine food

explanation.surface: Good food from a hilltop shop gives pleasure.
explanation.definitionFit: Great pleasure or joy is a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Mother's getting on with award of court

parts.note: a dam is the mother of an animal
to get on in years is to age

explanation.surface: An elderly mother wins compensation in court.
explanation.definitionFit: Damages are money awarded by a court as compensation.

clue.text: Over half a mile round is south Indian city's affectionate greeting

indicators.note: the kilometre letters go round the other pieces

parts.note: a kilometre, KM, is about 0.62 of a mile
taken as written
Agra is an Indian city, home of the Taj Mahal

explanation.surface: A loving greeting travelling half a mile around a southern Indian city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Over half a mile' is not a selection: a kilometre really is more than half a mile.

clue.text: Row caused by scientist or mathematician

indicators.note: the answer is produced by the letters running through these words

explanation.surface: An argument started by a scientist or a mathematician.
explanation.definitionFit: A storm is a violent outburst or row, as in a storm of protest.

definitions.meaning: a group of nine musicians or things
read as two words: no internet connection, so one cannot work online

explanation.definitionFit: A group of nine performers is called by this name, and split it reads no net.

clue.text: Half the folk next door sound like horses

indicators.note: half signals the first half of the word for the folk next door

explanation.definitionFit: Horses make a whinnying noise, which this verb names.
